documents.title: Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Roger is here for his diabetes and kidney check. Winter was quiet. He walked at the mall most mornings when the roads were bad. Log reviewed: fasting 120s to 160s, pre-supper similar, nothing below 80. He has not needed more than 4 units of aspart at any meal.
PA for the pens went through.
No chest discomfort, no shortness of breath, no foot sores, no swelling.

Exam: BP and weight per vitals. Comfortable. RRR. Clear lungs. No edema. Pedal pulses faint but present both sides, warm feet, skin intact.

Assessment and plan
Type 2 diabetes with CKD 3a: A1c and BMP today. Continue glargine 24 units and correction aspart.
Hypertension: continue lisinopril 10, amlodipine 5.
CAD/PAD: aspirin, atorvastatin 40.
Shingrix #2 due in May.
Next: wellness visit in June.

documents.title: Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
MEDICARE ANNUAL WELLNESS VISIT

Health risk assessment reviewed with patient. Lives in Hadley, independent in all daily activities, drives, manages his own medicines and insulin. No falls in the past year. Hearing adequate for conversation. Vision corrected, eye exam November 2023 without retinopathy.
PHQ-2: 0.
Cognition: Mini-Cog 3-word recall 3/3, clock normal.
Advance directive: has a health care proxy form at home, not yet filed; asked him to bring a copy.

Problems reviewed: HTN, T2DM on insulin with CKD 3a, hyperlipidemia, CAD s/p stent 2022, PAD (ABI 0.84 R / 0.78 L), former smoker.
Medications reconciled, unchanged.
Allergy: sulfa antibiotics.

Prevention:
- Colonoscopy 2018 normal; next 2028 if still appropriate.
- LDCT October 2023 Lung-RADS 1; next due this fall.
- AAA screen done 2023, normal.
- Immunizations: flu and PCV20 fall 2023, COVID 2023-24, Shingrix complete. RSV recommended this fall given diabetes and CKD.
- Hep C negative 2023.

Exam: well, BMI per vitals. Heart regular, lungs clear, no edema. Feet without lesions; pulses diminished bilaterally.

Plan: annual labs today. Diabetes follow-up in September. RSV and flu in the fall.

documents.title: Lab results from your wellness visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Mr. Wright, your labs from yesterday look stable. Kidney function is in your usual range, cholesterol is at goal on the atorvastatin, blood count is fine, and the urine protein check is normal again. A1c is in the same range as before. Nothing to change. See you in September.

documents.title: RE: Lab results from your wellness visit
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Thanks Doc. Will do.

documents.title: Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
SUBJECTIVE
Good summer. Sugars steady per his log, fasting mostly 130s-150s. No lows. Using aspart 2 units most suppers. No chest pain or pressure with yard work. No leg pain walking. No foot problems.

OBJECTIVE
Vitals reviewed. RRR, lungs clear, no edema. Feet: intact skin, diminished pulses as before, monofilament intact.

ASSESSMENT/PLAN
T2DM on insulin, stable. A1c, BMP today. Same doses.
HTN, CKD 3a: continue lisinopril/amlodipine. Labs as above.
CAD: due for cardiology in November.
RSV vaccine today (Arexvy), VIS given. Flu shot next month when the high-dose arrives.
LDCT due in October; reminder sent to scheduling.
RTC 3 months.

documents.title: Was in the hospital
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, wanted you to know I was in the hospital from last Friday till Tuesday. Had chest pressure Friday morning sitting at the kitchen table that would not quit so I called 911. They kept me and did a heart cath Monday through the left groin. They said no new stent was needed and to keep taking the same pills. They said I should see you and my heart doctor. I feel ok now. Groin is a little sore. Do you want to see me? Roger

documents.title: RE: Was in the hospital
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thank you for letting me know, Roger. Glad you are feeling better. Yes, I'd like to see you next week; the front desk will call with a time. We'll request the hospital records. If the chest pressure comes back, call 911 again, don't wait for us. If the groin gets more swollen, very bruised or painful, call the same day.

documents.title: Post-hospital follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen after an outside admission 9/27 to 10/1. Records requested 10/4, not yet received; history is from the patient and his discharge paperwork, which he did not bring.

He had resting chest pressure on 9/27 and called EMS. Admitted and told it was unstable angina. Diagnostic cath 9/30 through the left femoral artery; he was told no new stent was needed and to continue his current medicines. No chest pressure since discharge. Some soreness in the left groin that is fading. No leg pain, no numbness, no change in his feet.
Medicines unchanged: aspirin, atorvastatin 40, lisinopril 10, amlodipine 5, glargine 24, aspart scale.

Exam: comfortable. RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Left groin: puncture site healed, no hematoma, no bruit, no tenderness. Both feet warm, color normal, pulses diminished as at baseline.

A/P
1. Unstable angina, s/p diagnostic coronary angiography 9/30/2024, managed medically per patient. Continue aspirin and atorvastatin. He will move his cardiology follow-up earlier; their office is calling him. Chest pain precautions reviewed.
2. Left femoral access site healing well.
3. CKD 3a: BMP today after the hospital stay.
4. Will chase hospital records.
High-dose flu vaccine given today.

events.reason: left foot pain, discolored toe, kidney injury

procedures.procedure: Hospital discharge day management, 30 minutes or less

documents.title: Emergency department record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT PHYSICIAN RECORD
Patient: Roger Wright, 72M. Arrival 10/20/2024 13:25.

CC: Left foot pain x2 days.

HPI: 72-year-old man with diabetes on insulin, hypertension, CKD, hyperlipidemia, coronary disease with prior stent and peripheral arterial disease, who had a diagnostic heart catheterization for unstable angina three weeks ago. Two days of severe, sharp, constant pain in the left foot that gets worse when he props the leg up. Over the past couple of weeks he has also had brief spells of disturbed vision that clear on their own, and belly pain that comes on after meals.

HOME MEDS: insulin glargine 24 units at bedtime, insulin aspart correction scale with meals, lisinopril 10 mg daily, amlodipine 5 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg nightly, aspirin 81 mg daily.
ALLERGIES: sulfa antibiotics (rash).
FH: father MI at 64, mother ischemic stroke at 79, sibling with type 2 diabetes and kidney failure on dialysis.
SH: ex-smoker, 40 pack-years, quit 2022. No alcohol. Retired from the post office.

EXAM: Left foot cool compared with the right, one toe cyanotic. Lacy, net-like mottling over both lower legs. Fundoscopy: bright refractile plaques where retinal arterioles branch. Groin access site healed.

DATA: creatinine 2.8 mg/dL (his baseline 1.6), BUN 44, CBC within normal limits, CRP 46 mg/L, ESR 58 mm/h.

MDM: Blue toe, livedo, retinal cholesterol plaques and a sharp creatinine rise three weeks after a catheter procedure: cholesterol embolization syndrome with acute kidney injury. Admit to medicine for renal monitoring and pain control.

DISPOSITION: admitted.

documents.title: Hospital discharge summary
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted 10/20/2024. Discharged 10/23/2024.

Principal diagnosis: atheroembolism (cholesterol embolism syndrome) following coronary angiography 9/30/2024.
Secondary: acute kidney injury on CKD stage 3; type 2 diabetes on insulin; hypertension; coronary artery disease; peripheral arterial disease.

Hospital course: Presented with left foot pain, a cyanotic toe, livedo of the lower legs and retinal cholesterol plaques three weeks after femoral catheterization. Creatinine 2.8 on arrival from a baseline of 1.6. Managed supportively with fluids as tolerated, foot care and pain control. Aspirin and atorvastatin continued. No anticoagulation was given. Creatinine 2.5 on the morning of discharge. Foot pain improved; toe remained dusky but viable.

Discharge medications (no changes): insulin glargine 24 units at bedtime, insulin aspart correction scale, lisinopril 10 mg daily, amlodipine 5 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg nightly, aspirin 81 mg daily.
Allergies: sulfonamide antibiotics.

Follow-up: primary care within one week with a basic metabolic panel. Cardiology as scheduled.

documents.title: Post-discharge call
documents.author: RN
documents.body:
Patient called: discharged today from a second hospital stay since Sunday 10/20 for left foot pain and a blue toe. He says they told him small pieces of cholesterol broke loose after the heart cath and his kidneys took a hit. No discharge papers sent to us yet. Same medicines. Foot pain better than Sunday, toe still a bit purple. Eating and drinking ok, urinating normally. No chest pain.
Scheduled Monday 10/28 with PCP, bloodwork same day. Advised to keep the foot protected, no heating pad, and call or go to the ED for a black or open toe, fever, or much less urine.

events.reason: follow-up after hospitalization, atheroembolism and kidney injury

documents.title: Transitional Care Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
TRANSITIONAL CARE VISIT
Admission 10/20-10/23/2024. ED record received 10/25 and reviewed; discharge summary not yet received.

Summary from the ED record and patient: three weeks after the 9/30 diagnostic coronary angiography through the left femoral artery, he developed severe left foot pain, a cyanotic toe, livedo of both lower legs, retinal cholesterol plaques on fundoscopy, brief visual disturbances and post-meal belly pain. Creatinine 2.8 from baseline 1.6, BUN 44, CRP and ESR elevated, CBC normal. Diagnosed with cholesterol embolization and acute kidney injury. Told no medicine changes.

Today: foot pain much less, takes nothing for it now. Toe still dusky. Vision has been normal since the hospital. Belly pain after meals has settled. Urinating normally. Sugars a little higher in the hospital, back to his usual at home.

Exam: afebrile. Comfortable. Heart regular. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender. Legs: faint lacy mottling persists over both shins. One toe on the left foot dusky violaceous, cool at the tip, capillary refill slow, skin intact, no ulceration or black areas. Left foot otherwise warm. Pedal pulses diminished as before.

Creatinine today 2.3, coming down.

A/P
1. Atheroembolism (cholesterol embolism syndrome) after femoral catheterization, with acute kidney injury on CKD 3a. Supportive care. Continue aspirin and atorvastatin. Avoid any new vascular procedures if possible. Protect the foot. Recheck BMP in 3 weeks.
2. Unstable angina 9/2024 managed medically. Cardiology in December.
3. T2DM: same insulin.
4. Medication reconciliation done; list unchanged.
Call for any skin breakdown on the toe.

Called the hospital's records office again about the September admission and catheterization: they have no record of our 10/4 request. They asked for a new release; patient says he will sign one at his next visit. Closing the old request.

documents.title: Cardiology follow-up letter
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Re: Roger Wright, DOB 11/21/1951. Seen 12/11/2024.

Dear Doctor,

Mr. Wright returns after his September admission for unstable angina, during which diagnostic coronary angiography was done through the left femoral artery and he was managed medically. In October he was readmitted with cholesterol embolization and acute kidney injury, which you have been following.

He has had no angina since the angiography. He is walking again. No dyspnea, palpitations or syncope.

Medications: aspirin 81 mg, atorvastatin 40 mg, lisinopril 10 mg, amlodipine 5 mg, insulin glargine and aspart.
Allergies: sulfa antibiotics.

Exam: regular rhythm, no murmur. Lungs clear. No edema.
ECG: sinus rhythm, no acute ST or T change.

Assessment: coronary artery disease, stable since the September event. History of atheroembolism.
Plan: continue aspirin and atorvastatin 40 mg and his current blood pressure regimen. Follow-up in a year.

Outside cardiology
